column1: # Normalizers (CPORTS-HARNESS.md 4.3): NAME REGEX. The text each match covers,
# within one line, becomes "<n>" in both streams before comparison. Each is
# meant to cover only text that varies between runs, and each names the upstream
# line that prints it. What the harness checks (cports-matrix.py, Linux double
# run): the two raw Linux runs differ as a whole, their normalized forms are equal,
# and every pattern matches in both runs. It does not check that each pattern's
# own span differs between the runs (a span of random 0/1 is often equal by
# chance, so such a check would be flaky); that each span is variable text is
# established by the upstream line cited, and reviewed, not tested.
# lua-5.4.9-tests all.lua:59 random seeds
lua.all
# all.lua:111 memory figures (printed with leading spaces)
lua.all
# all.lua:146 per-file clock
lua.all
# math.lua:887 and :921: the numbers of the ranges drawn from the run's random seed (found by the
# harness's Linux double run); applied in order, so each later span sees the earlier <n>
lua.all
lua.all
lua.all
lua.all
lua.all
lua.all
# constructs.lua:348: GLOB1 = math.random(0, 1) (constructs.lua:317)
lua.all
# sort.lua:256 and :280: per-sort clock, and the comparison count of a randomly filled array
lua.all

# printed, and an unmatched pattern fails the run): all.lua:270 `^total time: .*$` and
# files.lua:947 `^test done on .*$`. They return with the final OK expectation (CPA-037).
